title: Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect (overview)
hook: Site-to-Site VPN encrypts traffic over the public internet between your data center and AWS. AWS Direct Connect (DX) provides a private network path with consistent latency — production hybrid designs almost always pair DX primary with VPN backup and BGP routing.

blocks.text: Site-to-Site VPN creates two redundant IPsec tunnels between a Customer Gateway (your router) and AWS — terminating on a Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) or Transit Gateway. Direct Connect is a dedicated or hosted Layer 2/3 circuit at an AWS Direct Connect location; Private Virtual Interface (VIF) reaches VPC or TGW, Public VIF reaches AWS public services without traversing the internet.

entries.plainDefinition: AWS resource describing your on-premises VPN endpoint and BGP ASN.
AWS-side VPN termination on a VPC — legacy; TGW preferred for multi-VPC.
DX logical interface carrying private RFC1918 traffic to VPC or TGW.
entries.example: VIF VLAN 100 to Direct Connect Gateway.

entries.plainDefinition: Dynamic routing protocol exchanging prefixes between on-prem and AWS.
entries.example: Advertise 172.16.0.0/12 from data center; AWS advertises 10.0.0.0/8.

blocks.text: Hybrid workloads — Active Directory, Oracle RAC stretch, mainframe batch — need predictable connectivity. VPN is quick to deploy; DX is the steady-state pipe. Senior interviews expect dual-tunnel VPN redundancy, BGP failover, and why DX plus VPN beats VPN-only for production.

blocks.title: HA pattern
blocks.body: Two VPN tunnels per connection; DX as primary with VPN backup; monitor BGP and tunnel telemetry, not just ping.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: VPN setup
items.body: Create CGW → VPN connection → configure router with AWS-provided IPsec → BGP or static routes.

items.title: DX setup
items.body: Order port or hosted connection → create Private VIF → attach Direct Connect Gateway to TGW.

items.title: Centralize on TGW
items.body: Modern designs terminate VPN and DX on TGW, not per-VPC VGW.

items.title: Failover
items.body: BGP withdraws failed path; backup tunnel or VPN carries traffic after convergence.

diagram.title: DX primary, VPN backup
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  DC[Data center] -->|IPsec| VPN[Site-to-Site VPN]
  DC -->|Private circuit| DX[Direct Connect]
  VPN --> TGW[Transit Gateway]
  DX --> TGW
  TGW --> VPC[VPC workloads]

snippet.label: CLI — VPN to Transit Gateway with BGP
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-customer-gateway \
  --type ipsec.1 --public-ip 203.0.113.10 --bgp-asn 65000

aws ec2 create-vpn-connection \
  --type ipsec.1 \
  --customer-gateway-id cgw-0abc \
  --transit-gateway-id tgw-0abc \
  --options StaticRoutesOnly=false
snippet.explanation: StaticRoutesOnly=false enables BGP. AWS creates two tunnels automatically for redundancy.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — Direct Connect Private VIF
snippet.code:
DxPrivateVif:
  Type: AWS::DirectConnect::VirtualInterface
  Properties:
    ConnectionId: !Ref DxConnection
    VirtualInterfaceType: private
    Vlan: 100
    AddressFamily: ipv4
    BgpAsn: 64512
    AmazonAddress: 169.254.10.1/30
    CustomerAddress: 169.254.10.2/30
    DirectConnectGatewayId: !Ref DxGateway
snippet.explanation: Private VIF pairs with Direct Connect Gateway for attachment to TGW or multiple VPC CIDRs.

snippet.label: CLI — VPN tunnel telemetry
snippet.explanation: Check UP/DOWN per tunnel before blaming application timeouts during maintenance.

snippet.label: CLI — DX connection health
snippet.explanation: Verify available state before troubleshooting BGP on the Private VIF.

blocks.title: Hybrid application paths
rows: Public VIF or VPN path to AWS APIs
SDK retries during BGP convergence matter
DX stable; VPN variable over internet
VPN may throttle large S3 uploads

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: NAT on-prem breaking IPsec identity. MTU/MSS mismatch causing silent TCP hangs. Static routes without monitoring backup tunnel during DX maintenance.

blocks.text: Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN uses AWS edge POPs for lower latency than standard VPN. DX has physical lead time — order early. True DX HA needs separate connections, not just dual VIFs on one port. How to prove it in production: CloudWatch VPN TunnelState metrics; DX ConnectionErrorCount; traceroute from on-prem shows DX path; capture BGP table during failover drill.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Internet jitter; not for 10G steady state
DX provisioning lead time and cost
Does not scale; TGW is modern hub

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying VPN and Direct Connect are interchangeable for production bulk transfer. Strong answer: VPN is IPsec over internet with variable path; DX is private circuit with committed bandwidth — combine for HA.

interviewTakeaways: Site-to-Site VPN: dual IPsec tunnels, terminates on VGW or TGW, BGP or static routes.
Direct Connect: Private VIF to VPC/TGW; Public VIF to AWS public endpoints — not the same as VPN.
Production hybrid: DX primary, VPN backup, BGP preference, quarterly failover drills.
60s: VPN = encrypted internet. DX = private line. Both attach to TGW in modern designs. BGP for failover. Monitor tunnel telemetry.
Follow-up: what breaks if only one VPN tunnel is UP?
commonPitfalls: Calling VPN just as good as DX for steady 10G replication — interviewers reject that; name latency and bandwidth commitments.
Strong answer: DX private path plus VPN backup with BGP; monitor both layers.
Single VPN tunnel treated as HA — AWS provides two tunnels; on-prem must use both.
Static routing without tested failover — silent outage when DX maintenance window starts.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript workers in a data center may reach AWS APIs over Public VIF while application traffic uses Private VIF to VPC — different paths like split-horizon DNS in corporate networks.
TypeScript DataSync or custom upload scripts should prefer DX path; implement retry with backoff during VPN failover when BGP converges.
